report.title: RUH & DMM Airport Status 3:00 AM AST: Riyadh HALTED, Dammam DISRUPTED
report.status_line: Airport halted since 8:10 PM, 410 minutes. No takeoff or landing since flynas XY278 from Sharm el-Sheikh at 8:10 PM (that landing ended the prior 2:05–8:10 PM halt of ~365 minutes). No takeoff since XY277 at 1:39 PM. GACA ops remain suspended after Saturday’s attack; GACA 12:46 AM follow-up: 12 fatalities and 309 injured. NOTAM A3586/26: AD NOT AVBL through 11 Oct 2100 UTC (midnight AST Monday). Coalition: attack is a terrorist act and will be responded to decisively; Al-Kharj ballistic intercept overnight. Cancellations remain elevated.
report.headline: Airport halted since 8:10 PM, 410 minutes — no takeoff or landing since XY278 at 8:10 PM; no takeoff since XY277 at 1:39 PM; GACA 12:46 AM: 12 dead, 309 injured; Coalition says terrorist act, will respond decisively; NOTAM A3586/26 still suspends ops through Sunday 2100 UTC; 518 flights cancelled today so far.
report.synopsis: There were 0 takeoffs in the last hour, the latest XY277 to Sharm el-Sheikh at 1:39 PM. The latest landing was XY278 from Sharm el-Sheikh at 8:10 PM, with 0 landings in the last hour. 518 flights are cancelled today (250 departures, 268 arrivals) and 2 arrivals have diverted. Yesterday, 9 October: 166 of 703 flights cancelled, 18 arrivals diverted and four halts of 45+ minutes, the longest 7:41 to 9:38 PM (no landing until 9:45 PM). No official reason has been given for the evening stop. Saturday morning: a 91-minute halt ran from 6:37 to 8:08 AM with no takeoff or landing. Saturday afternoon–evening: the board showed no takeoff or landing from 2:05 PM until flynas XY278 from Sharm el-Sheikh landed at 8:10 PM (~365 minutes). Since that landing there has been no further takeoff or landing — open halt since 8:10 PM (290 minutes at the 1:00 AM Sunday slot). Last takeoff remains flynas XY277 at 1:39 PM; prior last landing before XY278 was Air Cairo SM461 at 2:05 PM. GACA confirms King Khalid International Airport was attacked on Saturday afternoon and operations remain temporarily suspended until damage assessment and facility safety checks are complete. GACA follow-up statement at 12:46 AM Sunday (dated 11 October): the attack resulted in 12 fatalities — 4 Saudi citizens and residents of Bangladeshi (2), American (1), Egyptian (1), Jordanian (1), Syrian (1), Palestinian (1) and Sudanese (1) nationality — and 309 injured, including some in critical condition; property damage is being assessed. AIS/NOTAC shows NOTAM A3586/26 (NOTAMR) keeping the aerodrome unavailable from 10 Oct 19:24 UTC through 11 Oct 21:00 UTC. Flightradar24 at 11:35 PM reported Dammam-bound flights holding (including one originally for Riyadh); at 12:01 AM FR24 said flights were on approach to Dammam again. Reuters at 9:40 PM had restated the suspension with “several” wounded — GACA’s 12:46 AM tally supersedes that on casualties. AP reports an official saying a missile struck a passenger terminal and wounded many; AFP hospital source earlier said dozens injured / at least five Saudis in ICU; AFP diplomatic source said Houthis hit with a missile around 3:00 PM. Social-media death-toll claims circulating earlier remain unverified against the new official GACA figures. No official Houthi claim for Saturday found yet. Passengers told to confirm flight status before heading to the airport. Board cancellations remain elevated on Sunday 11 October.

airports_rule: Automatic status from the live Flightradar24 boards, 3-hour lookback. An official or NOTAM closure overrides everything. HALTED: an active closure, or 0 takeoffs/landings for 45+ minutes while 2 or more flights were scheduled in that window and none operated (cancelled, diverted, or more than 60 minutes past schedule with no actual time). QUIET (grey): 0 movements but fewer than 2 flights due, e.g. an overnight lull or published night closure; the next scheduled flight is shown. DISRUPTED: 15%+ of today's flights cancelled, any diversion today, a halt in the last 6 hours, or a night/partial NOTAM restriction. NORMAL: none of these. NO DATA: the board returned no rows. FR24 'Unknown' flights with no actual time count as due only once 60+ minutes overdue. When KSA Bot's editor level is given (blocks/airports.json), it is shown, marked 'editor', with the automatic status alongside.

strikes.title: Escalation pattern: Houthi strikes on KSA by target type
strikes.so_what: The campaign has climbed an escalation ladder: from military targets to economic targets (Aramco, Yanbu), then to symbolic targets (the Madinah power station serving the Prophet’s Mosque), and now to civilian aviation and the capital. King Khalid International Airport has now been hit or targeted on 19 Sep, 5, 7, 8 and 10 Oct; the 10 Oct strike closed it indefinitely, and a projectile fell near Dammam’s airport the same evening. Each rung raises the reputational cost to the Kingdom more than the military cost.

timeline.title: Timeline: incidents, events and official announcements

items.title: Houthis claim missile and drone strike on Aramco site in Riyadh
items.detail: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed ballistic missiles and drones hit an Aramco facility in Riyadh, causing fires; smoke was seen near an Aramco site south of the city.

items.title: Coalition calls Houthi Riyadh claims "misleading"
items.detail: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the Houthis were trying to divert attention from their losses.

items.title: Coalition: 97 strikes on Houthi reinforcements in Taiz
items.detail: The coalition said it carried out 97 precise targeting operations on the Tor al-Baha front and Taiz axis.

items.title: Jazan and Najran airports hit, 3 injured
items.detail: Saudi Arabia said 3 people were injured in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports as fighting with the Houthis reignited.

items.title: Houthis claim strikes on RUH and an Aramco refinery
items.detail: Explosions were heard in Riyadh; the Houthis claimed King Khalid airport and an Aramco refinery as targets.

items.title: Saudi–Turkey–Pakistan defence pact activated
items.detail: The mutual defence pact was activated after the Houthi attacks.

items.title: Air France, KLM, BA and Cathay Riyadh suspensions in force
items.detail: Air France and KLM suspended Riyadh (KLM also Dammam) to 24 Oct; BA resumes 1 daily flight on 3 Nov; Cathay suspended to 31 Jan 2027.

items.title: UK Embassy security alert; FCDO advice flags airports
items.detail: The UK issued an alert and updated travel advice on 6 Oct, after a US Mission alert on 5 Oct.

items.title: GACA: Abha airport attack, 2 killed, 28 injured
items.detail: Two women, a Moroccan and an Algerian, were killed at Abha International Airport.

items.title: GACA: KKIA attack, 1 killed, 8 injured
items.detail: A Sudanese man was killed at King Khalid airport; RUH traffic halted for over an hour.

items.title: Coalition: missile intercepted north of Riyadh
items.detail: The Houthis claimed a KKIA strike; the coalition said a missile was intercepted north of Riyadh.

items.title: GCC, Arab leaders and UN chief condemn airport attacks
items.detail: GCC and Arab leaders and the UN Secretary-General condemned the deadly attacks on Saudi airports.

items.title: Brent futures jump 4% to $104.28
items.detail: ICE Brent front-month rose from $100.20 on 7 Oct to $104.28 on 8 Oct.

items.title: Houthis claim ballistic missile on RUH; blast and evacuation
items.detail: AP witness reported a blast and evacuation; RUH traffic halted 12:25 to 2:18 PM.

items.title: Coalition: 2 missiles at Riyadh, 1 at Khamis Mushait intercepted
items.detail: Coalition statement after explosions were heard in the capital.

items.title: Smoke from a stationary aircraft at RUH
items.detail: Reuters reported smoke from an aircraft at the airport; the fire was put out. A parked Saudia jet was later reported heavily damaged.

items.title: Civil Defense: debris damaged a kindergarten and clinic
items.detail: Interception debris damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in Riyadh.

items.title: Houthis claim evening RUH strike with two cruise missiles
items.detail: Claim relayed from Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree.

items.title: Lufthansa Group and Air India suspend Riyadh flights
items.detail: Lufthansa Group suspended Riyadh to 16 Oct; Air India and Akasa to 10 Oct; IndiGo through 9 Oct.

items.title: Coalition: 82 Houthi targets destroyed
items.detail: Strikes in Saada, Hudaydah, Al-Jawf and Marib; al-Maliki said attacks on civilians "will not go unpunished".

items.title: US Mission issues security alert on RUH attacks
items.detail: US government staff later needed special authorisation to use Riyadh airport.

items.title: Hundreds of Riyadh flights cancelled
items.detail: Flightradar24 said airlines had cancelled hundreds of flights; more than 275 movements were reported cancelled on 8 Oct.

items.title: UK, France and UN condemn attacks
items.detail: Britain, France and the UN condemned the attacks on Abha and King Khalid airports overnight.

items.title: RUH halt 2:54–3:55 AM (61 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing for 61 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: RUH halt 5:19–6:26 AM (68 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing for 68 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: GACA: two Thursday attacks killed 3 Saudis; ops resumed
items.detail: Two attacks on 8 Oct hit KKIA facilities and a Saudia aircraft; Saudia named its pilot, Capt. Hamoud al-Kalthami, among the dead.

items.title: Coalition destroys 3 Houthi launch platforms
items.detail: Statement from the coalition spokesman.

items.title: PIA suspends Riyadh; Singapore Airlines defers launch
items.detail: Pakistan International Airlines suspended Riyadh flights; Singapore Airlines delayed its Riyadh route launch.

items.title: RUH halt 1:40–3:16 PM (96 min)
items.detail: Flightradar24 said the airport was closed again with no flights in the past hour, then open again at 3:18 PM.

items.title: DMM halt 1:47–3:07 PM (80 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing for 80+ minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: EASA widens conflict-zone warning for Saudi airspace
items.detail: EASA extended its conflict-zone bulletin covering Saudi airspace.

items.title: DMM halt 2:21–3:07 PM (46 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing at Dammam for 46 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: GCC and EU condemn RUH attacks
items.detail: The GCC called the attack a terrorist crime; von der Leyen pledged full EU solidarity.

items.title: Houthis warn all airlines in Saudi airspace
items.detail: The Houthis said all airlines flying in Saudi airspace are at risk.

items.title: Emirates, Etihad and flydubai cut UAE–Riyadh flights
items.detail: flydubai also cancelled Yanbu and Abha flights.

items.title: Houthis say flights to RUH need a Sanaa permit
items.detail: Yahya Saree said "humanitarian flights" to and from Riyadh need a permit from Sanaa.

items.title: RUH halt 4:05–4:50 PM (45 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing for 45 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: United States condemns attacks on Saudi airports
items.detail: The US condemned Houthi attacks on civilian infrastructure and airports; the UK also backed the Kingdom.

items.title: RUH halt 7:41–9:38 PM (117 min)
items.detail: Unverified posts reported explosions in Riyadh from 8:18 PM; Flightradar24 reported diversions, then flights heading back at 9:31 PM.

items.title: Civil Defense: do not film interception sites
items.detail: Warning against filming or sharing interception or debris sites; no shelter order.

items.title: 9 Oct: 166 of 703 RUH flights cancelled
items.detail: The day ended with 166 cancellations, 18 diversions and four halts of 45+ minutes. Brent futures closed at $104.72.

items.title: RUH halt 1:18–2:20 AM (62 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing for 62 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: Coalition: 136 Houthi military targets destroyed
items.detail: Statement carried by SPA.

items.title: DMM halt 5:29–6:25 AM (57 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing at Dammam for 57 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: RUH halt 6:37–8:08 AM (91 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing for 91 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: UAE condemns attacks on KKIA and Saudia aircraft
items.detail: UAE Foreign Ministry statement.

items.title: SriLankan suspends all Riyadh flights to 18 Oct
Air Arabia suspends Sharjah–Riyadh, Tabuk, Abha
items.detail: Suspension through Sunday 11 Oct.

items.title: DMM halt 1:46–2:36 PM (50 min)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing at Dammam for 50 minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: RUH halt from 2:05 PM; airport closed
items.detail: Last landing 2:05 PM; only one landing (flynas XY278, 8:10 PM) since. Inbound flights diverted, mainly to Jeddah.

items.title: Major Saudi conferences to proceed
items.detail: Organisers said major conferences would go ahead despite the airport attack.

items.title: Missile strikes RUH passenger terminal
items.detail: AFP witnesses heard a blast at about 3 PM and the airport was evacuated; AP quoted an official saying a missile hit a terminal.

items.title: KKIA advisory: check flight status with airline
items.detail: First official word after the halt; no reason given.

items.title: GACA confirms attack; RUH operations suspended
items.detail: Operations suspended until damage assessment and safety checks are complete; injuries being counted.

items.title: RUH halt since 8:10 PM (ongoing)
items.detail: No takeoff or landing for 343+ minutes (FR24 board).

items.title: NOTAM: RUH aerodrome not available
items.detail: "AD NOT AVBL due to precautionary measures", later extended by A3586/26 to 11 Oct 2100 UTC (midnight Riyadh).

items.title: DMM halt 10:29 PM–12:05 AM (96 min)
items.detail: Dammam-bound flights held away from the field, then approaches resumed at 12:01 AM.

items.title: 10 Oct: 316 RUH flights cancelled, 57 diverted
items.detail: Saturday ended with 316 cancellations (41%) and 57 diversions.

items.title: Palestinian Foreign Ministry condemns terrorist attacks on King Khalid International Airport
items.detail: Palestinian Foreign Ministry condemns the terrorist attacks on King Khalid International Airport.

items.title: Coalition: projectile fell near Dammam airport
items.detail: A projectile fell near King Fahd International Airport on Saturday evening.

items.title: GACA: 12 killed, 309 injured in RUH attack
items.detail: Dead include 4 Saudis and nationals of Bangladesh, the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan; operations remain suspended.

items.title: Gambia condemns Houthi attacks on the Kingdom
items.detail: Gambia condemns Houthi militia attacks on the Kingdom.

items.title: Cyprus strongly condemns Houthi attacks on King Khalid and Abha International Airports
items.detail: Cyprus Strongly Condemns Houthi Attacks on King Khalid and Abha International Airports.

items.title: GACA follow-up statement on the attack targeting King Khalid International Airport
items.detail: GACA Follow-up Statement on the Attack Targeting King Khalid International Airport.

items.detail: Coalition: interception and destruction of a ballistic missile in Al-Kharj province launched by the Houthi terrorist militia.

items.title: Coalition intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile in Al-Kharj province
items.detail: Coalition: interception and destruction of a ballistic missile in Al-Kharj province launched by the Houthi terrorist militia.

items.title: Muslim World League condemns continued Houthi attacks on the Kingdom and targeting of King Khalid International Airport
items.detail: The Muslim World League condemns the Houthi terrorist militia’s continued sinful attacks on the Kingdom and its targeting of King Khalid International Airport.

items.detail: Coalition: interception and destruction of a ballistic missile in Al-Kharj province launched by the Houthi terrorist militia; a projectile fell in the vicinity of King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

items.title: Al Ekhbariya: Coalition says KKIA attack is a war crime and will be answered decisively
